title: Microsoft Graph OAuth Business Write
goal: Implement delegated Microsoft Graph OAuth business-write support for customer-facing OpenCode and AnythingLLM MCP usage while forbidding send, delete, raw Graph, and application-permission access.
targetUsers: All acquired customers who use the Microsoft Graph MCP integration through OpenCode and/or AnythingLLM
constraints: Use delegated Microsoft user permissions only
Do not store tokens or secrets in OpenCode or AnythingLLM config
Do not expose direct email send, email delete, calendar delete, or raw Graph passthrough tools
Use a customer-facing MCP server name without unnecessary Pros branding, or document a compatibility alias
If Microsoft Graph implementation behavior is unclear or fails, read official Microsoft documentation before guessing
Attachment support must use extension allowlist, MIME validation, and conservative size limits
mustHave: OAuth setup and status for business-write-safe delegated scopes
OpenCode and AnythingLLM command-only MCP configuration
Calendar event create/update/invite with delegated shared calendar targets
Email draft create/update with delegated shared mailbox targets
Server-side confirmation gates for write operations
Tests for policy, forbidden operations, status states, attachments, shared targets, and MCP tools
Customer-facing documentation and runtime workflow updates
forbidden: Archive, binary, executable, script, source-code, and macro-office attachments

tasks.title: Graph-MCP kundentauglich benennen
acceptanceCriteria: Visible Microsoft Graph MCP server name avoids unnecessary Pros branding
Compatibility alias is documented if retained
Existing tests and evaluations are updated to the canonical name

tasks.title: OAuth-Scopes und Statusmodell auf business-write-safe erweitern
acceptanceCriteria: Microsoft Graph scopes include delegated mail draft and calendar write support
Status differentiates needs-auth, ready-read, ready-business-write-safe, limited, needs-reauth, and needs-admin-consent
No token or secret material appears in output

tasks.title: Graph-Safety-Policy implementieren
acceptanceCriteria: Allowlist and denylist are enforced server-side
Write operations require explicit confirmation
Delegated shared mailbox/calendar targets are validated
Send, delete, and raw Graph operations are impossible through exposed tools

tasks.title: Calendar Write Functions implementieren
acceptanceCriteria: Calendar events can be created with subject, time, timezone, body, location, and attendees
Calendar events can be updated without deletion semantics
Attendees can be added/invited
Shared calendar targets work when delegated permissions allow access
Ambiguous recurring event edits are rejected conservatively

tasks.title: Mail Draft Functions implementieren
acceptanceCriteria: Email drafts can be created without sending
Existing drafts can be updated only when the message is still a draft
Shared mailbox targets work when delegated permissions allow access
Non-draft update attempts are rejected

tasks.title: Draft Attachment Support implementieren
acceptanceCriteria: Allowed extensions include pdf, docx, xlsx, pptx, odt, ods, odp, txt, csv, tsv, png, jpg, jpeg, gif, and webp
Attachment validation checks extension, MIME type, and size limits
Archives, binaries, executables, scripts, source code, and macro Office files are rejected
Attachments can be added to drafts only

tasks.title: MCP Tools erweitern
acceptanceCriteria: Explicit schemas exist for calendar create/update/invite, draft create/update, and draft attachment tools
Write tools enforce confirmation input before Graph calls
Forbidden send/delete/raw tools are not exposed
Tool descriptions clearly state draft-only and no-send boundaries

tasks.title: OpenCode/AnythingLLM MCP Config erweitern
acceptanceCriteria: OpenCode can be configured with the Microsoft Graph MCP server
AnythingLLM can be configured with the Microsoft Graph MCP server
Client config contains only command and args, no secrets
Managed-state and doctor checks understand the Graph MCP entry

tasks.title: CLI/Doctor/Status UX aktualisieren
acceptanceCriteria: CLI help documents Graph auth/status/config flows
pros doctor reports Graph readiness and missing setup clearly
Status output explains limited scopes and reauth requirements
Admin-consent blocks are reported without exposing sensitive details

tasks.title: Tests ergänzen
acceptanceCriteria: Tests cover forbidden operations and missing confirmation
Tests cover draft-only updates and calendar recurrence rejection
Tests cover attachment allowlist and denylist
Tests cover shared mailbox/calendar target mapping and permission errors
Tests cover readiness states and no-secret client configs

tasks.title: Microsoft-Doku-Research Gate ausführen wenn nötig
acceptanceCriteria: Official Microsoft documentation is consulted for unclear Graph endpoints or failed implementation assumptions
Any documented behavior that affects implementation is recorded in progress notes or code comments where useful
No Graph behavior is guessed when blocked

tasks.title: README und Runtime-Workflow aktualisieren
acceptanceCriteria: Customer-facing setup explains OAuth, OpenCode, and AnythingLLM configuration
Allowed and forbidden actions are documented
Attachment allowlist and shared mailbox/calendar limits are documented
Runtime workflow reflects first-time Graph setup

tasks.title: End-to-end Smoke vorbereiten
acceptanceCriteria: Smoke covers first-time OAuth status path with no stored token
Smoke covers MCP status and safe draft/calendar flows with mocks or controlled Graph calls
Smoke verifies forbidden send/delete/raw operations are unavailable
Smoke verifies OpenCode and AnythingLLM config surfaces

doneWhen: Graph OAuth supports business-write-safe delegated scopes
Customer-facing Graph MCP naming is implemented or compatibility alias is documented
Calendar create/update/invite works with delegated user and shared calendar targets
Mail draft create/update and allowed attachments work with delegated user and shared mailbox targets
Direct send, email delete, calendar delete, and raw Graph passthrough are impossible through exposed MCP tools
OpenCode and AnythingLLM can be configured with command-only Graph MCP config
Tests cover safety policy and forbidden operations
Docs explain customer setup and safety boundaries
Unclear Microsoft Graph behavior is resolved by reading official Microsoft documentation

decisionLog.rationale: The work spans OAuth, Graph API, MCP tools, client configuration, tests, and docs with cross-boundary contracts.

decisionLog.decision: Use delegated Microsoft user permissions only
decisionLog.rationale: The user wants rights at the level of the signed-in user and no application-wide mailbox/calendar permissions.

decisionLog.decision: Forbid send, delete, and raw Graph operations
decisionLog.rationale: Direct sends and deletions are explicitly disallowed, and raw Graph would bypass safety policy.

decisionLog.decision: Research official Microsoft documentation when blocked
decisionLog.rationale: Graph behavior for drafts, attachments, shared resources, and recurrence can be subtle and must not be guessed.
